candidates.title: This smart ring tracks your sleep and becomes your AI note-taker when you’re awake
candidates.full_text:
Most smart rings are basically a glorified diary strapped to your finger. They sit there, log your heart rate and your sleep stages, and wait until morning to hand you a report card on a night you already lived through. Oura does it, Ultrahuman does it, RingConn does it, and they all do it well. Their main job is quietly collecting data, while giving you few ways to interact with the rings themselves. That’s the category in a nutshell, dozens of rings competing to be the most accurate silent observer of your life.

Interface, a new smart ring from Swiss hardware outfit Natura, the team behind Rolling Square, keeps that health data logging and adds an actual interface. Named rather aptly, it has a built-in button: press it, talk, and your words become a note, a message, or a request to your AI agents while your phone stays in your pocket. NatureOS connects the experience across iPhone, Android, Mac, and Windows. Heart rate and sleep tracking keep running in the background. The button gives you something to do with the hardware when a thought deserves recording as much as your pulse does.

Click Here to Buy Now: $159 $325 (51% off). Hurry, only 36/1660 left! Raised over $610,000.

Press and hold the button, speak, and release it to send a note, a message, or an AI request through NatureOS. Natura says you can whisper with the ring close to your lips in quiet settings, bring it closer in noisy surroundings, and talk normally the rest of the time. Whispering into your finger in a waiting room might earn a look, although so does talking to a watch. The button also activates dictation, putting your words wherever your cursor sits so you can reply without typing. One button, three jobs: recorder, dictaphone, and agent trigger.

Your chosen agent can work through connected apps, saving you the trip through five tabs to get something done. Natura says consequential actions wait for your approval. Inside NatureOS, you decide which apps each agent is allowed to access. That approval step matters when software can act on your behalf, particularly before anything sends or spends. Keeping a human in the loop before there’s a PR headache seems like a sensible arrangement. These permissions could decide whether you trust the gadget or quit it within a week.

Underneath the voice features sits the health-tracking hardware: Interface is designed to monitor heart rate, heart rate variability, blood oxygen, sleep, skin temperature, and activity throughout the day and night. Heart rate variability, or HRV, measures changes in the time between heartbeats and can help inform recovery estimates. Overnight tracking keeps collecting readings while you’re hopefully busy being asleep. Natura’s app mockups show resting heart rate and HRV trends, plus sleep broken into deep, light, REM, and awake stages. Those illustrate the intended experience, with the familiar charts joined by information you can speak into the ring yourself.

Log what you eat, your workouts, your supplements, or just how you feel, and the AI is designed to consider that alongside your biometrics. Typing all of this into an app after a long day feels like homework, and homework is the first thing anyone skips. Saying it out loud while mid-task could make the habit easier to keep. I find that a more interesting reason to put a microphone on a ring than simply having another place to summon an assistant. A late dinner or an unusually demanding workout gives a sleep chart some context, provided you remember to mention it.

Catch a thought before it’s gone: dictate an idea, a reminder, or a name, then find it later in NatureOS or have an agent organize it. Meetings get the fuller treatment, with recorded sessions turned into a transcript, speaker identification, and a recap of decisions and next steps. A small light stays on during recording, giving the person across the table a visible cue too. Meeting notes are the chore everyone agrees matters and nobody volunteers for, so handling the transcription and recap has an obvious appeal. At least your manager’s promises might make it into the minutes.

HumanPods, available in a bundle with the ring, are open-ear earbuds for asking agents questions, starting tasks, and hearing updates while your phone stays pocketed. Paired with Interface, they provide a way to hear a response after you’ve spoken a request. I can see the appeal: reaching for a screen to read every answer would interrupt the convenience of speaking in the first place.

candidates.title: 5 Smart Garage Door Openers You Control From Anywhere
candidates.full_text:
Adding phone control to your garage door can cost as little as $29.74 with the picks below, provided your existing opener is compatible. Four are retrofit controllers that keep your current motor; the Chamberlain replaces the entire machine.

All five offer phone-based control and door-status monitoring, but alerts, activity history, voice commands, and smart-home integrations vary by model. Start with compatibility, then compare the features and price.

Compatibility is the real fork in this table, since the meross only speaks Chamberlain-family protocols and the Konnected skips Security+ 2.0 doors. The sensors differ too, from a laser that watches the rolled-up door to a tilt switch that rides the door itself.

Every retrofit here leans on your home Wi-Fi or a hub, so a dead router leaves you with the wall button and the remote in the car. Old school, still works.

The MSG150HK is a smart remote that pairs with a compatible Chamberlain, LiftMaster, or Craftsman opener already listens for, so there’s no wired door sensor to mount and no adapter to hide. It speaks Security+ 1.0 and 2.0, plugs into Apple HomeKit, Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and CarPlay, and it carries no subscription fee. Renters, this is your pick.

Price: meross MSG150HK smart garage door opener remote, $59.49 (save $10.50, 15% off) Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

eKyro’s controller is the lowest-priced retrofit in this set, designed to add smart control to a wide range of existing garage-door openers, with an adapter required for some models. No monthly fee rides along. The box carries its own door sensors, mounting brackets, and hardware, and the listing promises scheduled checks that close a door left open and tell you about it.

Price: eKyro Smart Garage Door Opener, universal WiFi controller, $29.74 (save $5.25, 15% off) Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

At $29.74, it’s the cheapest way in this roundup to stop driving back home to check the door. Multi-door houses pair a second controller on the second door, and the app keeps both doors on one screen for the nightly lockup pass around the house.

YoLink ships a three-part kit: a garage door controller, a tilt sensor for the door itself, and a hub that plugs into your router and runs the show. Only the hub touches the internet. YoLink rates that link at a quarter mile in the open, which suits detached garages and metal buildings where the house Wi-Fi gives up.

Price: YoLink Garage Door Kit with controller, sensor, and hub, $47.99 (save $12.00, 20% off) Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

Alexa and Google handle voice, IFTTT and Home Assistant handle automations, and the sensor runs on two AAA batteries. Open-door alerts with your own time limits come standard in the app.

The C4310 is the one pick here that’s a whole new opener, a 3/4 HP chain-drive machine with a DC motor, a fixed camera, battery backup, two one-button remotes, and a multi-function wall control in the box. This is the replace-it-all option. Two-bulb lighting covers the front and back of the space, and the bulbs themselves are sold separately.

Price: Chamberlain C4310 chain drive myQ garage door opener, 3/4 HP with fixed camera, $204.00 (save $55.63, 21% off) Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

It weighs 31.8 pounds and carries a five-year motor warranty against one year on the chain, so this is a Saturday install with a helper, not a ten-minute clip-on. Dated opener, tired motor, no camera: this is the one that fixes all three. The battery backup keeps the door moving through an outage.

Konnected built the GDO White for people who want their garage inside a local hub, and it talks to SmartThings, Alexa, Home Assistant, Hubitat, Control4, and HomeSeer without a subscription or a battery to swap. The unit runs 2.75 by 1.9 inches, smaller than the wall remote it replaces. The GDO White supports local control through Home Assistant and Hubitat. Alexa and SmartThings integration uses Konnected’s free cloud service.

Price: Konnected Smart Garage Door Opener, white, $71.20 (save $17.80, 20% off) Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

The limit is the trigger: the GDO White fires openers with a push-button dry contact, so Security+ 2.0 doors need Konnected’s other model. At $71.20, it’s the priciest retrofit in the set.

candidates.title: This LEGO GTA VI diorama puts an entire speedboat getaway on your shelf
candidates.full_text:
Carly Rae Jepsen’s “Run Away With Me” came out in 2015, missed the Billboard Hot 100, and spent the next decade as the karaoke pick I’ll happily defend. Then Grand Theft Auto VI used it to score Lucia Caminos getting a taste of freedom after prison, jet ski and sax hook included. The song got a second wind on streaming eleven years later. It also happens to be the perfect soundtrack for this next bit: somebody built a GTA VI speedboat getaway in LEGO. Freedom, it turns out, snaps together in plastic bricks just fine.

That builder is hachiroku24, who started out tinkering with the GTA VI lettering. Then came a dock, a baffled cop, three palm trees, and a speedboat pitched up like it’s about to skip across the water. The giant brick-built logo looms behind the chase like a movie poster, pink and purple and completely unbothered by subtlety. Even the water gets a few shades of blue. You can tell where the boat’s been from the pieces bunched up behind it.

The dock has proper mooring bollards and a shark warning sign on a post. The patrol car is parked at the worst possible angle to catch anyone. The officer gets one job: watch Lucia and Jason speed off and look thoroughly unimpressed about it. Behind them, the GTA VI wordmark hangs like a title card nobody asked LEGO’s permission to print. A few details make this little patch of waterfront feel like part of a much bigger city.

Look under the speedboat and you’ll see upside-down slopes doing the work. They give the hull the angle it needs to look like it’s cutting through the water. The logo is mostly flat tiles, with a few turned on their sides to pick out the smaller details in the lettering. My favorite trick is hiding in the palm trees. Those ridged trunks are stacks of little LEGO crowns .

Back in 2022, hachiroku24 staged a brawl between Deadpool and Wolverine inside the X-Mansion , two years before their movie hit theaters. Then came a Portal 2 diorama on LEGO Ideas. Its GLaDOS, built from curved slopes and Technic pieces , looks like she’s about to insult you. The builder also made a Kraken display base for LEGO’s Black Pearl. It’s a good way to make a ship on a shelf look like it’s having a very bad day.

I like how often hachiroku24 picks the moment when something’s about to go wrong. Wolverine and Deadpool are already going at it. The Black Pearl is in the middle of a Kraken attack. Here, the cop has arrived just in time to watch the getaway. There’s something satisfying about a builder who sees a scene worth putting on a shelf and gets to work before anyone in licensing has booked a meeting.

Car theft, armed robberies, police chases: you can see why an official GTA VI set would be a tough pitch. Brick Fanatics pointed to the game’s realistic violence when it covered this build. LEGO Fortnite has had a little fun with GTA before. One promo even riffed on the game’s key art, right down to the pair leaning against a car by the beach. A cheeky poster is about as close as I’d expect the two to get.

I’d put “Run Away With Me” on for this one. It plays over a different scene in the game, but that sax hook suits the second the boat pulls away and the cop realizes his shift just got longer. The full build video on hachiroku24’s channel shows how the dock, the cop car, and the speedboat come together. Keep an eye on those palm trunks as they go up. Good luck seeing anything but crowns after that.
